newsitem.title: USA: J&L selects Pennsylvania site for melt-shop. [CORRECTED 19:06 GMT]
newsitem.headline: J&L selects Pennsylvania site for melt-shop. [CORRECTED 19:06 GMT]

text.p: J&L Structural Inc said Tuesday its directors voted to build a melt shop and continuous caster complex to supply the steel billet requirements for its rolling mill facility.

Subject to the successful completion of negotiations with Duquesne Light Co for electric power supply and the securing of an air quality permit from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection, a $45 million steelmaking facility will be constructed on 38 acres of land adjacent to its rolling mill facility in Aliquippa, Pa.

While much of the final engineering work on the project has been accomplished, "more work must be done now that a site has been selected. The start of construction will depend upon completion of final engineering and arranging financing for the project, including documentation for state financing."
The Aliquippa location choice was one of three options considered by the Board at its August 15 meeting, J&L said.
The other two considerations were construction of the complex in Columbiana County, Ohio, and pursuing a long-term billet supply agreement with one of its domestic suppliers.

"We have filed the required application for an air quality permit," J&L said. (Corrects to delete reference to J&L Specialty Steel Inc. J&L Structural Inc is a private company and is not related to J&L Specialty Steel Inc.)

"We need to see what effect if any, the new air quality regulations soon to be issued by the federal Environmental Protection Agency will have on our project and we need to complete the permitting process."

Beyond that, the company is in discussions with the Beaver County Corporation for Economic Development and DQE Inc's Duquesne Company to determine if the Aliquippa Port Authority qualifies as a municipality for purposes of electric power distribution and pricing.

"It is imperative that these discussions result in competitive electric power costs for the facility. Electrical energy will be the melt shop's second largest cost element behind ferrous scrap, and therefore, must be competitive," J&L pointed out.
The company noted it is in the final stages of start-up and commissioning of a new $8.5 million reheat furnace which commenced operation in July.
"We will now turn our attention to producing our own billets and, longer term, undertake further improvements to our rolling mill to expand our product offerings," it said.
